content.text:
I'm confirming the rename covers every caller by checking the graph's list against what I changed. Then I'll summarize.

I renamed `Subscription.getName()` to `getSubscriptionName()` in pulsar-broker. That covers the interface declaration and the two overrides, in `PersistentSubscription` and `NonPersistentSubscription`. `PulsarCompactorSubscription` and `AbstractSubscription` don't override it, so there was nothing to change there. I also updated every call site on a Subscription or subtype. Those are in `Consumer`, `ServerCnx`, `SharedConsumerAssignor`, `AbstractBaseDispatcher`, both `NonPersistentDispatcher*` classes, both delayed-delivery tracker factories, `PersistentTopic` (including the `PersistentSubscription::getName` method reference), `TransactionAggregator`, `MLPendingAckStoreProvider` and `PendingAckHandleImpl`. I left `getName()` alone on topics, cursors, dispatchers, managed ledgers and other types.

I found the call sites two ways. The first was the jQAssistant graph's list of callers of `Subscription.getName`. The second was grep for receivers named like a subscription, followed by a pass over the other `getName()` calls in the subscription classes. I didn't compile or run anything. A call on a receiver with an unusual name or an unusual call shape (for example a lambda or multi-line chain) could have been missed, and the compile check will show it. managed-ledger, pulsar-metadata, pulsar-common and pulsar-broker-common had no uses, so I changed nothing there.
